subject: Hosted API commit accelerator & soft rate tiers
messages:
From: Simon Knox <simon.knox@edgecommerce.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API commit accelerator & soft rate tiers

Hi Hannah,

We're deep into our usage planning for the next 12 months and expect a ~2.6x increase in token volume across peak campaigns. Our renewal is coming up on 2026-09-10 and we'd like to accelerate the commit ladder to secure better unit pricing while keeping a soft rate tier for burst months.

What we're looking for:
- Monthly committed tokens: increase from current 50M -> 150M (phased over 3 months)
- A soft burst tier (up to 220M/month) with a capped overage rate
- 12 month renewal term with an optional 6-month auto-review

Attached is our Q3 usage report and a draft SOW for the expanded scope. Can Redwood provide a proposed amendment with tiered unit pricing and any available churn credits for the early commit? We're also curious about SLA guarantees for dedicated throughput and whether burst credits are refundable if unused.

Procurement looped: procurement@edgecommerce.com

Thanks,
Simon Knox
Head of ML Platforms
EdgeCommerce

Attachments:
- EdgeCommerce_Q3_usage_report.csv (csv)
- Signed_SOW_draft.pdf (pdf)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Simon Knox <simon.knox@edgecommerce.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit accelerator & soft rate tiers

Hi Simon — thanks for the note and the usage file. This aligns with the activity we saw in your sandbox runs.

Quick next steps I propose:
1) I'll draft an amendment showing the phased commit increase + a soft burst ladder with capped overage rates.
2) Karthik will confirm operational feasibility for the burst cushion and any SLA addendum.
3) If procurement signs off, we'll route to legal for a short amendment and send a DocuSign link.

High-level: for a 3x commit increase we can offer a stepped unit price drop (see bullets below) + a one-time onboarding credit to offset migration throttling. I'll put numbers in the amendment and share by EOD tomorrow.

— Hannah

Hannah Schmitt

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-06T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit accelerator & soft rate tiers

On Thu, Aug 5, 2026 at 10:05 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Simon — thanks for the note and the usage file. This aligns with the activity we saw in your sandbox runs.

We can support the phased increase but need to lock a few operational knobs:
- Batching and KV cache tuning for long prompt workflows (we'll need expected 95th percentile seq length)
- Burst cushion: recommend a dedicated burst pocket equal to 40% of phased commit for the first 90 days
- Quantization profile: moving to int8 for LLMs will reduce GPU memory and lower cost; recommend pilot on non-critical models

If legal wants a hard SLA for burst throughput we should scope a separate SLO addendum; otherwise the soft-tier with capped overage is the smoother path.

I'll prepare an ops appendix to the amendment with the above items and a clear rollback plan.

— Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Simon Knox <simon.knox@edgecommerce.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@edgecommerce.com, Laura Pinto <laura.p@edgecommerce.com>
Date: 2026-08-07T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit accelerator & soft rate tiers

Thanks — the proposal looks good at a high level. Two quick asks before procurement signs:

1) Can we make the renewal term 15 months instead of 12 to align with our fiscal quarter cadence? (We'd accept a 15-month pricing table with a 6-month review clause.)
2) Please send the DocuSign link and an initial PO template so procurement can route internally.

We're ready to move once we have the DocuSign and a PO number. CC'ing procurement for visibility.

Best,
Simon
